    private readonly object _lock = new();
    // Sequence lock for Value: odd while a writer is replacing _state, even otherwise.
    private int _version;
    private global::Sample.ConfiguredState _state;

    public Store_Sample_ConfiguredState(System.IServiceProvider sp)
    {
        _state = global::Sample.ConfiguredState.Init(sp);
    }

    public global::Sample.ConfiguredState Value
    {
        get
        {
            // A struct wider than a pointer is copied field by field, so a copy that races a
            // writer can mix two states. Retry until the same even version is seen on both
            // sides of the copy: then no writer ran during it. Ordering: the first
            // Volatile.Read is an acquire, so the state loads cannot move above it. An
            // acquire does not stop earlier loads from moving below it, so volatile reads
            // alone could let the copy slip past the second version read.
            // Interlocked.MemoryBarrier is a full fence that keeps the copy above it.
            var spinner = default(System.Threading.SpinWait);
            while (true)
            {
                var before = System.Threading.Volatile.Read(ref _version);
                if ((before & 1) == 0)
                {
                    var state = _state;
                    System.Threading.Interlocked.MemoryBarrier();
                    if (System.Threading.Volatile.Read(ref _version) == before)
                    {
                        return state;
                    }
                }
                spinner.SpinOnce();
            }
        }
    }

    public event Action<global::Sample.ConfiguredState>? StateChanged;

    internal ValueTask UpdateAsync<TAction>(
        TAction action,
        Func<global::Sample.ConfiguredState, TAction, global::Sample.ConfiguredState> reducer)
    {
        global::Sample.ConfiguredState newState;
        lock (_lock)
        {
            newState = reducer(_state, action);
            // Only writers change _version, and they hold _lock, so the plain read of it is
            // current. Interlocked.Increment is a full fence: the state stores below cannot
            // move above the odd version. Volatile.Write is a release: they cannot move below
            // the even version either. A reader therefore never sees an even version around a
            // partly written state.
            System.Threading.Interlocked.Increment(ref _version);
            _state = newState;
            System.Threading.Volatile.Write(ref _version, _version + 1);
        }
        StateChanged?.Invoke(newState);
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }
